A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PS-Bench study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched despite layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety evaluations across five agent frameworks and five LLMs, intervention and personalization results, human evaluation, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark evaluations, intervention experiments, representation analysis, and appendix sensitivity tests.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedures, detection heuristics, reflective-reminder generation, and personalized inference procedure remain unchanged. Corrections from 'legitimization' to 'legitimation' do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LoCoMo-derived personas, 750 base queries, 1,986 persona-grounded queries, thematic augmentations, privacy probes, and representation-analysis datasets. The deployment scenarios added in Appendix F are discussed, not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged: LDAgent, A-mem, Mem0, MemOS, MemU, and stateless baselines, with the same subsets participating in the hard-query and intervention comparisons. Newly cited methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the reported backbone for Figure 4 from GPT-4o-mini to Qwen3-235B-A22B, matching the caption and Table 6 already present in v1. This is a limited configuration-reporting correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments; other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The thematic-memory, representation, privacy, memory-volume, explicit-persona, and intervention analyses are retained. Both case studies move from Appendix F to G without substantive changes. The new discussion supplies no additional experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 160-response human evaluation, two independent annotators, adjudication, and the same agreement-reporting procedure. No repeated-run, uncertainty, or significance-testing practice changes; the revised agreement percentage is a result change under E6.

E6.justification: Human–automatic evaluator agreement changes from 96.4% to 96.3% in Appendix B.2. The stateless Base Setting entries change from 19.00 to 23.13 in Table 5 and from 11.29 to 11.75 in Table 6, aligning them with Table 1. Other table results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The ASR definition and PCA-based reasoning remain unchanged, with no added or revised formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs. The new feedback-loop discussion is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: intent legitimation, PS-Bench, mechanistic evidence, and detection–reflection mitigation. The headline 15.8%–243.7% relative ASR increase is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix F substantially expands interpretation through a proposed persistent feedback loop and downstream risks in personal assistants, companion agents, and enterprise deployments. The limitations also explicitly exclude tool-augmented agents. These extend the applicability and risk discussion without new empirical validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository location in the abstract; v1 only states a future commitment to release data and evaluation protocols. Hardware, deployment arrangements, implementation descriptions, and substantive prompt contents remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning over-personalization, safety alignment, representations, and role-play safety, and elaborates comparison with role-playing jailbreaks in Appendix F.1. The original positioning around benign personalization rather than adversarial memory manipulation remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 removes repetition in Section 3.4, corrects terminology and cross-references, adds acknowledgments and a corresponding-author designation, and inserts a discussion appendix before the retained case studies. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures and 11 tables are retained. Appendix heatmaps and tables are repositioned, Table 8 persona labels lose the '_R3' suffix, and Figure 10's incorrect topic-relevance caption is replaced with an intent-legitimation description. The plotted graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves internal consistency through the Table 5–6 reference-value corrections, Figure 4 model attribution, and Figure 10 caption. Code-access information and the explicit tool-agent limitation improve transparency. The expanded discussion adds context, but its cumulative-feedback argument remains untested by the retained single-turn experiments, so the overall gain is limited.
